body.prompt:
Read the source notes of a legacy-data migration (below) and answer each setting from the notes only.
For each setting give its value from the allowed list and a quote: the one sentence of the notes that decides it, copied verbatim.
Use an empty quote only when the notes say nothing about the setting and the default applies.

Master convention: in the master file a positive amount means the customer or supplier owes us; a negative amount is a credit we owe them.

Settings:
- brightdesk_date_order: BRIGHTDESK numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- atlas_date_order: ATLAS numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- vendex_date_order: VENDEX numeric dates (birth and revision dates): does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- brightdesk_balance: BRIGHTDESK balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the customer (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if the printed sign already matches the master.
- atlas_owed: ATLAS "owed" figures: flip if a positive printed "owed" figure means we have to pay (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- ledgr_saldo: LEDGR Saldo: flip if a positive printed Saldo means we owe the account holder (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- kobo_balance: KOBO balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the member (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if a positive balance means the member owes us.
- kobo_trial: KOBO rows marked "flag: TRIAL": void if the notes say they must be dropped or are void; keep otherwise.
- brightdesk_void_stage: BRIGHTDESK: the value of the stage field whose rows are not real accounts and must stay out of the master (answer with that value only, e.g. the word after "stage="), or "" if no stage value is void.
- restamp_brightdesk: BRIGHTDESK update dates (the updated field): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy, restore, mirror or migration job re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_atlas: ATLAS update dates (last change): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_ledgr: LEDGR update dates (Geändert): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy job or migration rewrote them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_kobo: KOBO update dates (upd): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_veritas: VERITAS update dates (ts): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a mirror or copy re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.

NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR was migrated to new hardware between 21 December 2024 and 1 February 2025, and the migration overwrote Geändert on every row with the migration date.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Numeric birth dates in ATLAS use the same order as BRIGHTDESK (only the separator may differ). Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates use the same order as BRIGHTDESK. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

body.prompt:
IDENTITY RULES (section 3 of the specification):
3. Identity. Two rows describe the same person when
   (a) both give a birth date, the dates are the same calendar day once each row's date is read in its own system's convention, and the names match (3.1); or
   (b) at least one of the two gives no usable birth date, the names match, and both carry the same phone number after E.164 normalisation.
   A person is a group of rows linked by such matches (chains count). Rows whose birth dates differ are different people even when their names are identical — namesakes exist. A shared phone number on its own (for example a household line) does not make two people one.
   3.1 Names match when, ignoring letter case, the system's name order, titles and salutations, middle initials, spaces and apostrophes: the given names are equal once a nickname is replaced by its formal name (appendix A), the family names are equal, an accented letter counts as equal to its ASCII rendering (listed in section 4), and at most one typing error in total is tolerated across given and family name together (one letter wrong, missing or extra, or two adjacent letters swapped). Two different ASCII renderings of one accented letter (for example "u" and "ue" for "ü") are not equal to each other; that difference counts as a typing error.



For each pair decide same: true only if the rules make them one person. Give shared_quote: the shared attribute copied verbatim from one of the two records.

body.prompt:
Read the source notes of a legacy-data migration (below) and answer each setting from the notes only.
For each setting give its value from the allowed list and a quote: the one sentence of the notes that decides it, copied verbatim.
Use an empty quote only when the notes say nothing about the setting and the default applies.

Master convention: in the master file a positive amount means the customer or supplier owes us; a negative amount is a credit we owe them.

Settings:
- brightdesk_date_order: BRIGHTDESK numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- atlas_date_order: ATLAS numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- vendex_date_order: VENDEX numeric dates (birth and revision dates): does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- brightdesk_balance: BRIGHTDESK balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the customer (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if the printed sign already matches the master.
- atlas_owed: ATLAS "owed" figures: flip if a positive printed "owed" figure means we have to pay (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- ledgr_saldo: LEDGR Saldo: flip if a positive printed Saldo means we owe the account holder (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- kobo_balance: KOBO balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the member (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if a positive balance means the member owes us.
- kobo_trial: KOBO rows marked "flag: TRIAL": void if the notes say they must be dropped or are void; keep otherwise.
- brightdesk_void_stage: BRIGHTDESK: the value of the stage field whose rows are not real accounts and must stay out of the master (answer with that value only, e.g. the word after "stage="), or "" if no stage value is void.
- restamp_brightdesk: BRIGHTDESK update dates (the updated field): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy, restore, mirror or migration job re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_atlas: ATLAS update dates (last change): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_ledgr: LEDGR update dates (Geändert): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy job or migration rewrote them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_kobo: KOBO update dates (upd): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_veritas: VERITAS update dates (ts): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a mirror or copy re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.

NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR was migrated to new hardware between 21 December 2024 and 1 February 2025, and the migration overwrote Geändert on every row with the migration date.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Numeric birth dates in ATLAS use the same order as BRIGHTDESK (only the separator may differ). Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates use the same order as BRIGHTDESK. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

IDENTITY RULES (section 3 of the specification):
3. Identity. Two rows describe the same person when
   (a) both give a birth date, the dates are the same calendar day once each row's date is read in its own system's convention, and the names match (3.1); or
   (b) at least one of the two gives no usable birth date, the names match, and both carry the same phone number after E.164 normalisation.
   A person is a group of rows linked by such matches (chains count). Rows whose birth dates differ are different people even when their names are identical — namesakes exist. A shared phone number on its own (for example a household line) does not make two people one.
   3.1 Names match when, ignoring letter case, the system's name order, titles and salutations, middle initials, spaces and apostrophes: the given names are equal once a nickname is replaced by its formal name (appendix A), the family names are equal, an accented letter counts as equal to its ASCII rendering (listed in section 4), and at most one typing error in total is tolerated across given and family name together (one letter wrong, missing or extra, or two adjacent letters swapped). Two different ASCII renderings of one accented letter (for example "u" and "ue" for "ü") are not equal to each other; that difference counts as a typing error.



For each pair decide same: true only if the rules make them one person. Give shared_quote: the shared attribute copied verbatim from one of the two records.

- atlas_date_order: ATLAS numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- vendex_date_order: VENDEX numeric dates (birth and revision dates): does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- brightdesk_balance: BRIGHTDESK balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the customer (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if the printed sign already matches the master.
- atlas_owed: ATLAS "owed" figures: flip if a positive printed "owed" figure means we have to pay (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- ledgr_saldo: LEDGR Saldo: flip if a positive printed Saldo means we owe the account holder (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- kobo_balance: KOBO balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the member (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if a positive balance means the member owes us.
- kobo_trial: KOBO rows marked "flag: TRIAL": void if the notes say they must be dropped or are void; keep otherwise.

- restamp_atlas: ATLAS update dates (last change): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_ledgr: LEDGR update dates (Geändert): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy job or migration rewrote them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_kobo: KOBO update dates (upd): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_veritas: VERITAS update dates (ts): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a mirror or copy re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.

NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR was migrated to new hardware between 21 December 2024 and 1 February 2025, and the migration overwrote Geändert on every row with the migration date.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Numeric birth dates in ATLAS use the same order as BRIGHTDESK (only the separator may differ). Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates use the same order as BRIGHTDESK. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

3. Identity. Two rows describe the same person when
   (a) both give a birth date, the dates are the same calendar day once each row's date is read in its own system's convention, and the names match (3.1); or
   (b) at least one of the two gives no usable birth date, the names match, and both carry the same phone number after E.164 normalisation.
   A person is a group of rows linked by such matches (chains count). Rows whose birth dates differ are different people even when their names are identical — namesakes exist. A shared phone number on its own (for example a household line) does not make two people one.
   3.1 Names match when, ignoring letter case, the system's name order, titles and salutations, middle initials, spaces and apostrophes: the given names are equal once a nickname is replaced by its formal name (appendix A), the family names are equal, an accented letter counts as equal to its ASCII rendering (listed in section 4), and at most one typing error in total is tolerated across given and family name together (one letter wrong, missing or extra, or two adjacent letters swapped). Two different ASCII renderings of one accented letter (for example "u" and "ue" for "ü") are not equal to each other; that difference counts as a typing error.

"Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

body.prompt:
Read the source notes of a legacy-data migration (below) and answer each setting from the notes only.
For each setting give its value from the allowed list and a quote: the one sentence of the notes that decides it, copied verbatim.
Use an empty quote only when the notes say nothing about the setting and the default applies.

Master convention: in the master file a positive amount means the customer or supplier owes us; a negative amount is a credit we owe them.

Settings:
- brightdesk_date_order: BRIGHTDESK numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- atlas_date_order: ATLAS numeric birth dates: does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- vendex_date_order: VENDEX numeric dates (birth and revision dates): does the month or the day come first? MDY = month first, DMY = day first.
- brightdesk_balance: BRIGHTDESK balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the customer (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if the printed sign already matches the master.
- atlas_owed: ATLAS "owed" figures: flip if a positive printed "owed" figure means we have to pay (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- ledgr_saldo: LEDGR Saldo: flip if a positive printed Saldo means we owe the account holder (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep otherwise.
- kobo_balance: KOBO balances: flip if a positive printed balance means we owe the member (so its sign must be inverted for the master); keep if a positive balance means the member owes us.
- kobo_trial: KOBO rows marked "flag: TRIAL": void if the notes say they must be dropped or are void; keep otherwise.
- brightdesk_void_stage: BRIGHTDESK: the value of the stage field whose rows are not real accounts and must stay out of the master (answer with that value only, e.g. the word after "stage="), or "" if no stage value is void.
- restamp_brightdesk: BRIGHTDESK update dates (the updated field): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy, restore, mirror or migration job re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_atlas: ATLAS update dates (last change): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_ledgr: LEDGR update dates (Geändert): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a copy job or migration rewrote them); "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_kobo: KOBO update dates (upd): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates; "reliable" otherwise.
- restamp_veritas: VERITAS update dates (ts): "restamped" if the notes say they are not real change dates (a mirror or copy re-stamped them); "reliable" otherwise.

NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Numeric birth dates are MM/DD/YYYY, as everywhere in the US sales organisation, even for European customers. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=migrated with stage=customer rows: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, Ireland. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR was migrated to new hardware between 21 December 2024 and 1 February 2025, and the migration overwrote Geändert on every row with the migration date.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Numeric birth dates in ATLAS use the same order as BRIGHTDESK (only the separator may differ). Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates use the same order as BRIGHTDESK. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

Each system has an update-date field (BRIGHTDESK updated, LEDGR Geändert, ATLAS last change, VENDEX revision date, KOBO upd, VERITAS ts). For each system BRIGHTDESK, LEDGR, ATLAS, VENDEX, KOBO, VERITAS, do the notes say that its update dates are NOT real change dates (for example because a migration, mirror, copy or restore job re-stamped/overwrote them)? Answer true only if the notes say so; quote the deciding sentence verbatim from that system's paragraph (empty string when the notes say nothing, or when they say the dates are reliable you may quote that).

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "inaktiv" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 16 April 2025–14 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

Each system has an update-date field (BRIGHTDESK updated, LEDGR Geändert, ATLAS last change, VENDEX revision date, KOBO upd, VERITAS ts). For each system BRIGHTDESK, LEDGR, ATLAS, VENDEX, KOBO, VERITAS, do the notes say that its update dates are NOT real change dates (for example because a migration, mirror, copy or restore job re-stamped/overwrote them)? Answer true only if the notes say so; quote the deciding sentence verbatim from that system's paragraph (empty string when the notes say nothing, or when they say the dates are reliable you may quote that).

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Numeric birth dates are MM/DD/YYYY, as everywhere in the US sales organisation, even for European customers. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=migrated with stage=customer rows: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, Ireland. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances keep their sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"import" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. This VERITAS extract comes from a read-only mirror that was rebuilt between 29 November 2024 and 12 January 2025: the ts value of every VERITAS row is the time the mirror copied it, not the time the record last changed.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Numeric birth dates are MM/DD/YYYY, as everywhere in the US sales organisation, even for European customers. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=migrated with stage=customer rows: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances keep their sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. Rows marked "env":"import" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

Each system has an update-date field (BRIGHTDESK updated, LEDGR Geändert, ATLAS last change, VENDEX revision date, KOBO upd, VERITAS ts). For each system BRIGHTDESK, LEDGR, ATLAS, VENDEX, KOBO, VERITAS, do the notes say that its update dates are NOT real change dates (for example because a migration, mirror, copy or restore job re-stamped/overwrote them)? Answer true only if the notes say so; quote the deciding sentence verbatim from that system's paragraph (empty string when the notes say nothing, or when they say the dates are reliable you may quote that).

Numeric birth dates are MM/DD/YYYY, as everywhere in the US sales organisation, even for European customers. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Numeric birth dates are MM/DD/YYYY, as everywhere in the US sales organisation, even for European customers. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=migrated with stage=customer rows: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances keep their sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. Rows marked "env":"import" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. This VERITAS extract comes from a read-only mirror that was rebuilt between 29 November 2024 and 12 January 2025: the ts value of every VERITAS row is the time the mirror copied it, not the time the record last changed.

The export contains rows carrying these status markers (system, marker as it appears in the row):
0. LEDGR: Status=storniert
1. LEDGR: Status=gesperrt
2. VERITAS: "env":"import"
3. LEDGR: Status=aktiv
4. VERITAS: "env":"production"
5. BRIGHTDESK: stage=migrated
6. BRIGHTDESK: stage=customer
7. KOBO: flag: SAMPLE
8. VERITAS: "env":"sandbox"

For each marker decide, from the notes only, whether a row carrying it is VOID (a test/demo/cancelled/withdrawn/not-real row that must not be migrated) or KEEP (a real account, or the notes do not describe it as void). For a VOID marker give the sentence of that system's paragraph that says so (verbatim). For KEEP give the deciding sentence if the notes mention it, else an empty string.

SOURCE NOTES:

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

In the master list a positive amount means the person owes us money; a negative amount is a credit (we owe them).
For each system BRIGHTDESK, LEDGR, ATLAS, KOBO, VERITAS: take a balance figure written in that system as a plain positive number with NO negative marker (no minus, no parentheses, no "CR", no "▲"). Does the master record it as POSITIVE or NEGATIVE? Follow the system's paragraph (e.g. "prints balances the opposite way", "changes sign", "keeps its sign", "is a credit").
