Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=migrated does not carry a void marker; keep it. BRIGHTDESK was migrated to new hardware between 18 January 2025 and 20 February 2025, and the migration overwrote updated on every row with the migration date.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR never re-stamps rows: its Geändert always shows the true date of the last change.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"backfill" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR was migrated to new hardware between 21 December 2024 and 1 February 2025, and the migration overwrote Geändert on every row with the migration date.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Numeric birth dates in ATLAS use the same order as BRIGHTDESK (only the separator may differ). Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates use the same order as BRIGHTDESK. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. VERITAS never re-stamps rows: its ts always shows the true date of the last change.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "inaktiv" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 16 April 2025–14 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

The export contains rows carrying these status markers (system, marker as it appears in the row):
0. VENDEX: (Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)
1. LEDGR: Status=gesperrt
2. LEDGR: Status=aktiv
3. VERITAS: "env":"production"
4. BRIGHTDESK: stage=customer
5. LEDGR: Status=inaktiv
6. LEDGR: Status=storniert
7. KOBO: flag: SAMPLE
8. KOBO: flag: TRIAL

For each marker decide, from the notes only, whether a row carrying it is VOID (a test/demo/cancelled/withdrawn/not-real row that must not be migrated) or KEEP (a real account, or the notes do not describe it as void). For a VOID marker give the sentence of that system's paragraph that says so (verbatim). For KEEP give the deciding sentence if the notes mention it, else an empty string.

SOURCE NOTES:

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

body.prompt:
SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Treat rows marked Status "archiviert" exactly like "storniert" entries.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-receivable ledger: "owed" is money due to us, and a "CR" figure is money we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: DORMANT" are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances change sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. KOBO's upd is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2022 audit.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 23 May 2025 and 21 June 2025 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

8833: Supplier contact Björn Sjöberg (DOB the 2nd of July 1950), based in Denmark; best number +45 90 31 90 08; no balance recorded. Entry revised March 29, 2022.

For each entry return:
- id: the entry id.
- given, family: the person's given name and family name exactly as spelled in the entry, without titles (Mr, Dr, Prof, ...) and without middle initials. Family name particles (van der, de, ...) belong to the family name.
- dob_quote: the birth date expression exactly as written (e.g. "04/05/1975", "October 11th, 1993", "the 12th of June 2000", "05-Sep-59"), without leading words like "born"/"DOB"/"b."; "" when the birth date is unknown or not on file.
- phone_quote: the phone number exactly as written; "" when there is none.
- balance_quote: the amount with its currency exactly as written (e.g. "USD 7,092.73", "twenty-five thousand four hundred sixty-nine euros and seventy cents", "one hundred pounds sterling"), without the lead-in words; "" when no balance is recorded.
- balance_kind: OWES_US for "owes us"/"open balance"/"outstanding"/"balance due"; CREDIT for "in credit by"/"holding a credit of"/"credit balance of"/"we owe them"; NONE when there is no balance.
- revised_quote: the date the entry was revised exactly as written (for "Spoke with <name> on <date>" it is the call date).
- country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (United Kingdom = GB) of the country the person is in, from a named country, a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" = NL) or the city they are based in; "" if the entry gives no such cue. A phone calling code is NOT a country cue.
- country_cue: the exact words of the entry that give the country (the country name, adjective or city); "" when country is "".

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "inaktiv" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 16 April 2025–14 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: TRIAL" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=migrated does not carry a void marker; keep it. BRIGHTDESK was migrated to new hardware between 18 January 2025 and 20 February 2025, and the migration overwrote updated on every row with the migration date.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR never re-stamps rows: its Geändert always shows the true date of the last change.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). The slashes may look American, but ATLAS birth dates are not month-first: the day comes first. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Read "owed" literally: it is the amount the supplier still has to pay us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"backfill" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list.

Each system has an update-date field (BRIGHTDESK updated, LEDGR Geändert, ATLAS last change, VENDEX revision date, KOBO upd, VERITAS ts). For each system BRIGHTDESK, LEDGR, ATLAS, VENDEX, KOBO, VERITAS, do the notes say that its update dates are NOT real change dates (for example because a migration, mirror, copy or restore job re-stamped/overwrote them)? Answer true only if the notes say so; quote the deciding sentence verbatim from that system's paragraph (empty string when the notes say nothing, or when they say the dates are reliable you may quote that).

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=migrated does not carry a void marker; keep it. BRIGHTDESK was migrated to new hardware between 18 January 2025 and 20 February 2025, and the migration overwrote updated on every row with the migration date.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. LEDGR never re-stamps rows: its Geändert always shows the true date of the last change.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). The slashes may look American, but ATLAS birth dates are not month-first: the day comes first. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Read "owed" literally: it is the amount the supplier still has to pay us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"backfill" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list.

For each of BRIGHTDESK, ATLAS and VENDEX: in a fully numeric date such as 04/05/1975, which comes first, the day or the month? Resolve cross-references (e.g. "same order as BRIGHTDESK") and worked examples (e.g. "dob=11/02/1996 is 2 November 1996" means MONTH_FIRST). Quote, verbatim, the sentence of that system's own paragraph that decides it.

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=01/07/1992 is 7 January 1992. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances are prepaid deposits we hold for the customer, not open invoices, so the master records them with the opposite sign. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. stage=review marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 13 September 2024 and 23 October 2024, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS is a UK ledger, but its birth dates are not day-first: the month comes first. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team works from Pittsburgh and writes numeric dates the way people there do. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is prepaid store credit, which we owe the member (negative in the master); "▲" or a minus marks a member who owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"import" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped.

The export contains rows carrying these status markers (system, marker as it appears in the row):
0. LEDGR: Status=aktiv
1. VERITAS: "env":"import"
2. BRIGHTDESK: stage=customer
3. VERITAS: "env":"production"
4. VERITAS: "env":"sandbox"
5. BRIGHTDESK: stage=review
6. LEDGR: Status=gesperrt
7. VENDEX: (Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)

For each marker decide, from the notes only, whether a row carrying it is VOID (a test/demo/cancelled/withdrawn/not-real row that must not be migrated) or KEEP (a real account, or the notes do not describe it as void). For a VOID marker give the sentence of that system's paragraph that says so (verbatim). For KEEP give the deciding sentence if the notes mention it, else an empty string.

SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. SOURCE NOTES:

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the British order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=migrated does not carry a void marker; keep it.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS was configured in US locale, so numeric birth dates are month/day/year, not day/month/year. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what the supplier owes us, not what we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Oslo to Raleigh in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances change sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: GUEST" were opened by the auditors to test the system, whatever the label suggests; leave them out. KOBO's upd is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2019 audit.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 29 November 2024 and 27 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

0. ATLAS: DO NOT MIGRATE
1. LEDGR: Status=aktiv
2. KOBO: flag: GUEST
3. BRIGHTDESK: stage=customer
4. VENDEX: (Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)
5. VERITAS: "env":"sandbox"
6. VERITAS: "env":"production"
7. BRIGHTDESK: stage=migrated

For each marker decide, from the notes only, whether a row carrying it is VOID (a test/demo/cancelled/withdrawn/not-real row that must not be migrated) or KEEP (a real account, or the notes do not describe it as void). For a VOID marker give the sentence of that system's paragraph that says so (verbatim). For KEEP give the deciding sentence if the notes mention it, else an empty string.
